items.title: Satellite images show smoke near Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline
items.summary: Satellite images show smoke near Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline Satellite images showed smoke rising near Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, one of the kingdom’s key energy assets, Reuters has reported. The news agency said Saudi authorities did not immediately report any incident at the site. The East-West Pipeline has become increasingly important for Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, enabling state oil giant Aramco to ship crude from the kingdom’s eastern coast to the Red Sea on its western coast. It offers an alternative route for sending crude through the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic global energy chokepoint. BIG: Satellite imagery shows a massive smoke plume (~100 km long) and sustained thermal hotspots along Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline corridor southeast of Medina. items.summary: Iranian arms and advice helped Yemen's Houthis seize key Red Sea city, sources say The lightning Houthi advance down Yemen's Red Sea coast this week came with direct guidance from Iran's Revolutionary Guards seeking to open a new front in US-Israeli war on Iran, according to Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources. Iran told the Houthis last week to escalate their attacks on Saudi Arabia, a close US ally, and promised more funding, weapons and senior officers to help them do so, two Iranian sources said. Several senior Revolutionary Guards commanders had already travelled to Yemen to oversee and command Houthi attacks directed against Saudi Arabia after weeks of discussions over military strategy, a regional diplomat briefed by Tehran said. A third Iranian source, an official, said Iran had held several meetings with allies including the Houthis and that the move on Mocha was a Houthi rather than Iranian decision. However, it had helped Iran by putting upward pressure on oil prices and hurting the United States and Saudi Arabia, the official added. Reporting by Reuters

items.summary: Iranian strikes damaged multiple aircraft at Jordan base, report says Iranian strikes damaged multiple American military aircraft this week on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, a US official told Reuters. The US military, the highest-funded in the world, suffered material damage even before Iran's strikes on Tuesday. This includes the destruction of more than two dozen drones, Iran striking fighter jets, and aircraft being lost to accidents. According to a May report from the Congressional Research Service, 42 US military aircraft had already been lost or damaged in the conflict. Since the Iran war started in February, 18 US service members have been killed and over 800 injured. A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said Iran's attack hit one A-10 Thunderbolt II, known as the Warthog, leaving it with a missing wing, while roughly eight F-15s sustained light damage and were returned to service. Iran's strike on the US base in Jordan came after US forces said they destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers. Report by Reuters

The ministry asserted that Tehran remains determined to "firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests" against US actions, including Washington's ongoing maritime blockade, attacks on commercial vessels, and its continued "economic war". "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stresses that responsibility for the consequences arising from the continuation of US aggressive and interventionist actions in the region will rest with the US regime and its accomplices and partners," it added.

items.title: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon
items.summary: US diesel prices hit record $5.85 a gallon The price of diesel hit a new record Friday in the United States, as disruption from the US war with Iran squeezes voters. The cost is now $5.85 a gallon, up from $3.71 a year ago, the AAA motorists' association said. Diesel is used by farmers to run equipment, and it also powers the trucks needed to bring food to grocery stores. US farmers faced a double whammy of surging fertiliser and diesel prices as the spring planting season got underway. The Independent Grocers Alliance estimates that fuel-related costs can account for 15 to 30 percent of the total cost for some food products. Besides diesel, the cost of regular gasoline is also notably higher at an average of $4.15 per gallon, compared with $3.20 last year. (Reporting by AFP)

items.summary: US diesel prices hit all-time high because of Iran war Drivers in the US are paying more than ever for diesel at the pump as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to hit ordinary citizens at home. In the US, diesel is mostly used by commercial vehicles, such as trucks, trains, boats, buses, farming vehicles and construction vehicles, the BBC reported. The average price for one gallon of diesel in the US has hit $5.85, compared to an average of $3.71 a year ago and above the previous high following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the American Automobile Association said. Fuel prices have soared since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran at the end of February, reflecting the surge in wholesale oil prices. In response to rising fuel costs, US President Donald Trump recently pledged to “substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans” through an oil deal with Venezuela, after the US kidnapped the country's former president Nicolas Maduro then supported his successor Delcy Rodriguez.

items.summary: Hormuz will remain under Iran's full control, Baghaei says Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, has said the Strait of Hormuz remains and will remain under Iran’s full control, blaming the US for regional maritime insecurity and rising global fuel prices, Mehr news agency reported. “The insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is the result of US actions, and if the international community is concerned about rising fuel prices, it should reprimand the United States,” Baghaei said during a televised interview on Friday. Baghaei accused the United States of violating the Islamabad MoU only 23 days after its signing, adding the US’s “pretexts” for carrying out attacks “had no basis”.

items.title: Iran used Chinese satellite images for attack on US base in Jordan
items.summary: Iran used Chinese satellite images for attack on US base in Jordan Iran used Chinese satellite images to carry out its attack on an American base in Jordan that killed three US troops in July, The Wall Street Journal reported. Citing US officials familiar with details of the incident, the newspaper reported that Tehran had acquired high-resolution satellite images of Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, which suffered extensive damage in the strike. The newspaper reported that US officials declined to identify the Chinese entities that supplied the imagery to Iran and did not allege direct involvement by Beijing.

items.summary: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports Top White House advisers, including vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio, have privately warned president Donald Trump that the conflict with Iran could extend through the remainder of his presidency, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials. The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The advisers told Trump in private discussions in the Oval Office and the Situation Room that Tehran could continue to resist US pressure, potentially prolonging the conflict beyond Inauguration Day in January 2029, the Journal added. The reported warning contrasts with Trump's own public remarks about the war. The president said on Wednesday he expected the war to end "immediately after" the US midterm elections in November, arguing that Iran was trying to influence the vote but would be unable to sustain its resistance much longer. Trump also acknowledged diplomatic talks are still a possibility but were not preferred. Report by Reuters

items.title: Amerikaans vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln verlaat Thailand
items.summary: Het Amerikaanse vliegdekschip USS Abraham Lincoln is na vijf dagen vertrokken uit Thailand. Bijna 5000 bemanningsleden zijn meer dan negen maanden na hun vertrek uit de Verenigde Staten onderweg naar de haven van San Diego. De afgelopen vijf dagen lag de Lincoln in de Thaise haven Laem Chabang, dicht bij de badplaats Pattaya. De badplaats is Amerikaanse soldaten niet onbekend: tijdens de Vietnamoorlog werd het een bekende plek voor het zogenoemde R&R ( Rest and Relaxation) , oftewel: een vakantie voor militairen. De badplaats had daarvoor voorbereidingen getroffen: er werd onder meer een prostitutieverbod ingesteld en er werden extra agenten ingezet. Lokale verslaggevers melden dat het bezoek relatief soepel is verlopen. Soldaten genoten van voetspa's, winkelen en roomservice. Volgens persbureau AFP zijn twee leden van het leger teruggestuurd naar het schip na een dronken ruzie. Uitgeputte bemanning Het schip vertrok op 21 november uit San Diego, voor een missie die vier tot vijf maanden zou duren. Dat werd het dubbele door de oorlog die de VS met Iran begon. items.summary: Underwater drone capture gives Tehran opportunity to reverse engineer vessel Iran's capture of a US military underwater drone gives Tehran an opportunity to study and potentially reverse engineer the vessel, delivering a setback for the Pentagon and drone maker Anduril. The US military and Anduril have downplayed the significance of the drone falling into Iranian hands. The vessel, a Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle designed for long-range surveillance and other undersea missions, is among a new generation of military drones intended to operate for days with little human intervention. Washington has previously treated the loss of advanced drones to Iran as a serious matter. After Iran captured an RQ-170 Sentinel stealth reconnaissance drone in 2011, then-President Barack Obama publicly asked Tehran to return the aircraft. Iran later claimed it had reverse-engineered the drone and subsequently unveiled domestically produced models that appeared to draw heavily on its design. items.title: Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US
items.summary: Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US Donald Trump said on Friday that the Iran war was "small potatoes" for the United States, in his administration's latest bid to play down the war ahead of crucial midterm elections. Trump's comments came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that "I wouldn't call it a war" despite an upsurge in clashes between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz. "A lot of people don't call it a war. I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Vance's remarks. "It's not a big thing. We did Venezuela, and we did this," added Trump, who was surrounded by cattle ranchers invited for the signing of two executive orders on beef processing.

items.summary: Middle East crude oil exports in August down 39 percent, TankerTrackers says Crude oil exports out of the Middle East during August 2026 were down 39 percent since the January and February baseline of 18.5 million barrels per day (mbpd), according to oil-tracking firm TankerTrackers. The sharpest fall of 67 percent below pre-war levels was recorded in May, the firm said, adding that the current deficit is now only 7.2 mbpd, compared with 12.4 mbpd in May. The firm covered Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Oman, the UAE and Qatar in its assessment.

Tehran described the strikes as part of Washington’s wider military campaign and “economic war” against Iran. It said the attacks violated the UN Charter and endangered international peace, security and commercial shipping. The ministry pledged to “firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests” against US aggression, state-sponsored terrorism, the continuing blockade and the “harassment of commercial ships”. It added that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from continued US “aggressive and interventionist actions” in the region.

If passed, the resolution would follow up on one adopted on June 12 of last year declaring Iran in breach of its non-proliferation obligations for not fully cooperating with an investigation into uranium traces found at undeclared sites. Israel started bombing Iran's nuclear facilities the next day, soon joined by the US Iran's uranium-enrichment plants were destroyed or badly damaged. Iran has not let International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors return to the bombed sites since then or verify what remains of its stocks of enriched uranium, some of which was enriched to up to 60 percent purity, a short step from weapons grade. clusters.headline: Witkoff & Kushner to spend Labor Day weekend in Russia, Ukraine

items.title: Witkoff & Kushner to spend Labor Day weekend in Russia, Ukraine
items.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will reportedly travel to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend in an effort to revive negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. It will mark the diplomatic duo’s first trip to Kyiv since President Donald Trump’s return to office, and follows CIA director John Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow last week. “It is unclear whether the Americans are bringing new proposals to the two presidents, or are pushing them to close the gap on the remaining issues, which include who will ultimately control the Donbas, Ukrainian territory that is partly occupied by Russia,” according to a New York Times report. George Beebe, director of grand strategy at the Quincy Institute, called the development “most welcome” and said all parties had strong reasons to find a way to end the fighting. He cautioned, however, that “seizing this propitious moment will require overcoming deep mistrust between the two countries” and addressing doubt that the “Trump administration has the political clout and persistence to overcome opposition in Europe and inside the Washington establishment.”

items.title: Witkoff and Kushner to visit Russia and Ukraine at weekend, says Tass
items.summary: Witkoff and Kushner to visit Russia and Ukraine at weekend, says Tass US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine on Saturday and Sunday, Russian news agency Tass reported, citing a source. There was no immediate confirmation. Witkoff and Kushner last visited Moscow in January, when they held four hours of late-night talks with President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin, Reuters reported. The two men are also US President Donald Trump's lead negotiators on Gaza and the war on Iran. If the visit takes place it will be their first to Kyiv. “The Russians don't want them to visit Kyiv and are trying to make them change the plan,” the source told the Russian news agency. The last US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine took place in February, shortly before the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran.

items.title: Can 'America First' survive Trump's war-first presidency?
items.summary: In a Thursday address at the GOP midterm convention that exalted President Donald Trump and demeaned his opponents as “extremists who openly hate our nation,” Vice President JD Vance hardly spoke about foreign policy. He did not mention the war in Iran directly, and he only brought up foreign policy as an example of an issue that divides the party’s base. He urged voters not to “throw the baby out with the bathwater” because “you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here or there.” The acknowledgement of foreign policy as a divisive issue in the MAGA coalition is a stark retreat for Vance, who staked his 2023 endorsement of Trump on the fact that “he started no wars despite enormous pressure from his own party and even members of his own administration,” framing the president’s America First record as a much-needed deviation from decades of bipartisan hawkishness. clusters.headline: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'?

items.title: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'?
items.summary: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'? A quarter century is enough time to separate history from hysteria, consequences from intentions and reality from propaganda. On 11 September 2001, nearly 3,000 people were killed in horrific attacks that shocked the United States and the world. The attacks of 9/11 could have been treated as a grave crime requiring an international effort to identify, apprehend and prosecute those responsible. They could also have triggered a serious national debate about why such intense hostility towards the US had developed in many parts of the Muslim-majority world. Instead, the US's political establishment chose a radically different path. President George W Bush famously declared that the terrorists attacked the US because "they hate our freedoms". It was a convenient explanation because it absolved the American foreign policy establishment of any responsibility. items.title: Iran president says he does not favour continuing the war
items.summary: Iran president says he does not favour continuing the war Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he does not support continuing the war, but he stressed that Iran needs to improve its resistance to future challenges so that it does not have to negotiate from a position of weakness. Speaking to heads of the country’s leading universities, Pezeshkian said universities should support the government across areas including the economy, management, culture and literature, ISNA reported. Pezeshkian also called for greater involvement of students in tackling national issues. “We must make sure that instead of engaging in protest, they engage in solving problems,” he said. The president said he had “no political angle with anyone”, adding, “Whoever helps us solve the country’s problems, with whatever political viewpoint, I accept.” “Economic measures must take into account the country’s conditions, otherwise they will lead to negative results and losses instead of addressing the issues,” Pezeshkian said.

Volgens Israël is met de aanval "de operationele controle van de Ali Taher-heuvelrug bereikt, zowel bovengronds als ondergronds". Het leger bracht beelden naar buiten van de explosie: Bij de aanval werd 1100 ton aan explosieven gebruikt, meldt het Israëlische leger. De schokken waren voelbaar in heel Zuid-Libanon en zelfs in de hoofdstad Beiroet, die op ongeveer 70 kilometer afstand ligt. The meeting would be the first between the top diplomats from the six-member Gulf Cooperation Council and a senior Iranian official since the US and Israel launched the war against Iran in February. The last time Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi attended a GCC gathering was October 2024 in Doha. Scheduled to be held in the Omani coastal city of Salalah, the details of the meeting were not finalised, but a number of states had confirmed and it was expected to go ahead, the report said, citing two people in know of the development. “For Iran and Oman it is about getting the GCC on board to try and use that to get the US to lift its blockade on Iranian ports,” said one of the people briefed on the matter. items.title: Milei has staked it all on Trump. Will he follow through?
items.summary: The territorial dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands (or Islas Malvinas in Spanish) continues to escalate. Last week, Argentine President Javier Milei, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, announced a series of new measures aimed at pressuring Britain over the future of the islands. The most significant announcement was of new sanctions on companies involved in oil extraction in the waters around the Falklands, which Argentina has long claimed as its own. Argentina’s attempt to prevent the exploitation of the Falklands’ natural resources is a reminder that beneath the often farcical relitigating of sovereignty claims dating back to the 18th century is a very modern geopolitical conflict with real stakes for energy and maritime resources. Yet what was most remarkable about Milei’s announcement was what Milei did not announce — namely, a shift in U.S. policy regarding the Falklands. items.summary: De Houthi's in Jemen hebben de havenstad Mokka ingenomen. Dat meldt persbureau Reuters, op basis van militaire bronnen van de Jemenitische regering. De inname van de stad markeert de grootste verschuiving van de frontlinies in vier jaar tijd. Vorige week begonnen de Houthi's, die worden gesteund door Iran, een offensief met vermoedelijk als doel om controle te krijgen over Bab el-Mandeb, de belangrijke zeestraat tussen Jemen en de Hoorn van Afrika. In de afgelopen dagen wonnen de Houthi's al flink terrein, met onder meer de herovering van de stad Hais, gisternacht. Niet ver daarvandaan ligt de stad Mokka. Vanochtend verschenen de eerste beelden vanuit de stad. Op beelden die de NOS verifieerde zijn onder meer Houthi-strijdkrachten te zien bij een verlaten voertuig van het Jemenitische staatsleger. Wie zijn de Houthi's? Dat en vier andere vragen leggen we in dit artikel aan je uit. Mokka is een strategisch gelegen havenstad aan de Rode Zee, iets ten noorden van de zeestraat. clusters.headline: Olivier Grondeau, ancien otage en Iran : «La poésie, c'est ce qui m'a fait tenir»

items.title: Olivier Grondeau, ancien otage en Iran : «La poésie, c'est ce qui m'a fait tenir»
items.summary: Olivier Grondeau a passé deux ans et demi en prison en Iran. Son nom est moins connu que ceux d’otages dont le cas a été médiatisé. Son histoire est assez proche. Arrêté à Chiraz le 12 octobre 2022, à l’époque des manifestations suivant la mort de Jina Mahsa Amini, il a été libéré en mars 2025. Il n’avait décidé de parler de sa situation que quelques mois plus tôt. Olivier Grondeau est un voyageur à tout petit budget, un poète, un grand lecteur, un ancien champion de scrabble. C’est son esprit, son humour, son imagination qui l’ont aidé à tenir. Il le raconte dans un livre publié chez l’iconoclaste : « Joseph dans la nuit »

items.title: Political Instability Meets Fiscal Limits: Is France the Euro’s Next Big Stress Test?
items.summary: With around half a year remaining before the next presidential election, France is in danger of becoming a stress test for the eurozone: a political crisis, a deteriorating fiscal position and growing market doubts about the country’s ability to finance its mounting debt burden are all converging. France faces a significant structural imbalance in its public finances. The budget deficit exceeds 5 per cent of GDP , while public expenditure stands at around 57 per cent of GDP. At the same time, public debt is rising steadily and could, without sufficient fiscal consolidation measures, exceed 130 per cent of GDP by 2030 . The interest burden on public debt is rising rapidly and could rise to more than 120 billion euros, equivalent to 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2030. The central challenge, however, may not lie in the fiscal arithmetic of the budget, but in the political capacity to address it. items.summary: While it is somewhat cliche to say that the “whole world changed” after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, it does not detract from the reality of the statement. In numerous tangible ways, the culture, security, and politics of the nation were never the same after al-Qaida hijackers in passenger planes left nearly 3,000 people dead in smoldering ruins across lower Manhattan, the Pentagon, and a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. For many of us who lived through it all, a quarter century has passed in a blink, while at the same time the pre-9/11 Washington era paradoxically seems so far away, and perhaps softened a bit by wistfulness and nostalgia. Conversely, the “post” era is pockmarked by wars, and an expansion of the national security state that was unimaginable a generation ago. Those born too early to witness the events of that day know nothing other than the current atmosphere of hyper-securitization and political polarization. Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a post on X that disruptions from attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities were used as a pretext to refer Iran to the Security Council, adding that the move will not "achieve anything". clusters.headline: How Congress gave up its power over war and peace

items.title: How Congress gave up its power over war and peace
items.summary: In 1973, after it was discovered that the U.S. had secretly bombed Cambodia, Congress took action. In an effort to assert its power over matters of war and peace, Congress pushed through the War Powers Resolution despite then-President Richard Nixon’s veto, and it has been law ever since. Unfortunately, congressional enforcement of the War Powers Resolution has been mixed. In 2026 alone, Congress has put forward some 19 war powers resolutions in an attempt to rein in hostilities in Iran, Venezuela, Cuba, and Lebanon. So far, none of these resolutions has stopped a conflict. Take Iran, for example. There have been eight votes to end the war, seven of which failed. Just one of these passed and only because Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) changed course after losing his primary to a challenger endorsed by President Donald Trump, giving him leeway to vote against the bulk of the Republican Party. Cassidy’s move highlights one of the main problems with the War Powers Resolution: too many of our elected officials cast votes for political gain, not American interests. items.summary: Bij een luchtaanval op een gevangenis in het noorden van Jemen zijn zeker 23 mensen om het leven gekomen. Reddingswerkers hebben vandaag vier lichamen geborgen uit het puin van de gevangenis, die maandag instortte na een aanval van de door Saudi-Arabië geleide coalitie. De gevangenis stond in de strategisch gelegen stad Hazm, in de provincie Jawf. Volgens de Houthi's wordt nog gezocht naar zeven vermisten. Bij de aanval raakten zeker zeven mensen gewond. Onder hen was een vrouw die haar echtgenoot in de gevangenis bezocht. De identiteit van de dodelijke slachtoffers is nog niet vastgesteld. De aanval maakt deel uit van een nieuwe escalatie van het conflict in Jemen. De door Saudi-Arabië geleide coalitie voerde vanochtend nieuwe luchtaanvallen uit op militaire doelen van de Houthi's in de provincies Marib en Jawf. De Houthi's reageerden eerder met een reeks raket- en droneaanvallen op het zuiden van Saudi-Arabië. Daarbij raakten volgens de autoriteiten 73 mensen gewond. Shallah*, then 16, watched the news at home on the Afghan TV channel Tolo news. She ran crying to the garden, to tell her mother that Afghanistan had fallen. Her younger sister, Fatimah*, then 11, was at her cousin’s house, where her aunt told her the news. At the time, she says, she did not understand what a takeover meant, or who the Taliban were. items.title: Vat olie boven de 100 dollar, ook benzineprijs blijft stijgen
items.summary: Na de nieuwe aanvallen van de Verenigde Staten en Iran zijn de olieprijzen opnieuw gestegen. De prijs van een vat Brent-olie kwam vanochtend boven de 100 dollar uit. Dat is voor het eerst sinds juli. Een vat Brent-olie is inmiddels bijna 60 procent duurder dan begin dit jaar. Door de aanvallen tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran is er onrust op de oliemarkt. Het aanhoudende geweld vergroot de zorgen over mogelijke verstoringen van de olie-export uit de regio. De Amerikaanse bank Goldman Sachs heeft gewaarschuwd dat de olieprijs kan oplopen naar 120 dollar per vat als de aanvallen aanhouden. De stijgende olieprijs is ook al te merken aan de pomp. De adviesprijs voor een liter benzine ligt nu rond de 2,72 euro.

clusters.headline: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États

items.title: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États
items.summary: La sortie mondiale du pétrole pourrait entraîner des conflits, des migrations et des bouleversements économiques selon une étude du groupe de réflexion E3G publiée mardi 8 septembre. L’utilisation du pétrole est en déclin dans de nombreux pays, avec la croissance des énergies renouvelables, et les effets de la guerre en Iran qui a limité l’offre et fait flamber les prix. Et cette stagnation va obliger les producteurs à rechercher un bassin d’acheteurs en déclin. Des pays comme le Nigeria, l’Iran, l’Angola et l’Algérie font partie des pays qui seront gravement touchés, car ils dépendent fortement des revenus pétroliers pour financer leurs services publics. Sans aide internationale, ils ne pourront pas amortir le choc alertent les experts.

items.title: Goederenvervoer binnenvaart flink lager door droogte
items.summary: De lage waterstanden deze zomer waren een groot probleem voor de binnenvaart. In augustus is er bijna 19 procent minder gewicht aan goederen vervoerd dan een jaar eerder. Dat blijkt uit cijfers van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS). Door de aanhoudende droogte daalde de vaardiepte, waardoor schepen minder zwaar beladen konden worden. In totaal werd er 21,8 miljoen ton vervoerd. Dat is het laagste vervoerde gewicht in de maand augustus in de afgelopen vijftien jaar. In augustus bedroeg het gemiddelde gewicht per schip zo'n 1299 ton, terwijl dat normaal rond de 1500 ton ligt. Het is niet de eerste keer dat het vervoerde gewicht in de binnenvaart fors afneemt door lage waterstanden: dit gebeurde in 2018 en 2022 ook. Verschillen Naar bijna elk land werd er minder vervoerd via de binnenvaart. Het vervoer tussen Nederland en Duitsland nam het sterkst af. Er ging bijna 40 procent minder gewicht aan goederen naar Duitsland, en omgekeerd kwam er voor een kleine 50 procent minder naar Nederland. items.title: Hegseth has been a disaster. It's time for Trump to fire him.
items.summary: It’s hard to determine who is more under siege today – the mullahs of Iran or the U.S. secretary of defense who is prosecuting the war against them. For months, negative stories about Secretary of War Pete Hegseth have peppered major newspapers. These include everything from his seeming “war on DEI” within the department, to combative engagements with members of Congress, to shade being thrown even by President Donald Trump himself on the lack of success in the (second) Iran War. As the midterms loom, one wonders if the president is ready to pull the plug on Hegseth in an attempt to distance himself from the failure of the Iran war. President Trump should have pulled the plug long ago. On November 12, 2024, I went on NBC News when Hegseth had been announced as Trump’s nominee for secretary of defense and argued that Hegseth might be just what we need, instead of another standard military-industrial-complex ‘veteran’ who never met a war he didn’t like. clusters.headline: Trump denials can't hide billions in US weapons sent to Ukraine

items.title: Trump denials can't hide billions in US weapons sent to Ukraine
items.summary: Trying to pin the blame for the depletion of U.S. military stockpiles on something other than the war in Iran, President Donald Trump fell back on a usual scapegoat last week: Ukraine. “The Biden administration gave far more munitions away to Ukraine, at no cost to them whatsoever, than we have used in Iran,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. This is a familiar refrain. Trump loves to remind his audience that because of him, Americans are “not spending on Ukraine anymore” and instead, Europe is footing the bill. In truth, most people in the United States don’t think about Ukraine much these days. But since Trump himself brought it up, it’s worth asking: What exactly is going on with U.S. military support to Ukraine? The answer might surprise you. Despite Trump’s rhetoric, the United States remains deeply embroiled in Ukraine’s ongoing conflict with Russia in ways that create national security risks and run counter to Trump’s own foreign policy goals. They then traveled to Kyiv for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said the pair presented him with some "worthwhile ideas." Yet, as the war drags closer to five full years of fighting, chances of success at the negotiating table appear slim. Don’t hold your breath for an end to the Ukraine war before the midterms in November. More likely, Putin will continue to shift the goalposts until he achieves his core goals: Ukrainian neutrality and the political decapitation of Zelensky. More than a year has passed since President Donald Trump met with Putin in Anchorage. The Trump Administration has been unable to deliver upon the compromises offered at that summit. clusters.headline: 25 years after 9/11, the US still doesn't know 'why they hate us'

items.title: 25 years after 9/11, the US still doesn't know 'why they hate us'
items.summary: Twenty-five years ago, 19 hijackers took control of four American airliners and crashed them into symbols of American power, killing upwards of 3000 people. The American population watched the events unfold in real time. It was an emotionally jarring event that changed the country. In some respects, the events of 9/11 needed no explanation. The destruction of the World Trade Center buildings and the massive, and random, loss of life were horrifying to all. The meaning of the attacks, however – and the motivations of the hijackers – were less clear. The effort to explain the motives behind the attack, and to understand “why they hate us,” brought a pre-existing debate over Islamist militancy to the center of American public life. In the decade leading up to 9/11, the Washington policy community had been divided over how to deal with the Islamist movement and particularly those extremists who sought to use violence to impose a narrow vision of religious orthodoxy upon reluctant societies. clusters.headline: Somali piracy was under control. Then came the Iran war.

items.title: Somali piracy was under control. Then came the Iran war.
items.summary: From the start, the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has been a story of unintended consequences. Contrary to President Donald Trump’s hopes for a quick victory, the conflict has morphed into a sustained crisis, one that has driven up oil prices, driven down tourism in the Middle East, and reshaped the region’s geopolitical map. Now, a new unintended consequence has emerged: the return of piracy to Somalia’s coasts. This shift, which comes after a decade of quiet, threatens some of the world’s most important shipping lanes and the interests of the United States and its allies. Pirates have attacked at least 15 vessels in the region this year, a sharp uptick from the five attacks that occurred last year, according to data from the International Maritime Organization. The renewed criminal activity has led to extended hostage situations, including one ongoing seizure of an oil tanker and its crew. A controversial operation to free the MV LATUF, carried out by Somali forces and the Turkish navy late last month, raised questions about whether a ransom was paid. items.title: Hijacking pirates exploit regional chaos to return to seas off Somalia
items.summary: US-Israel war on Iran and political instability in Somalia lead to pirates targeting cargo ships off Horn of Africa The scourge of Somali piracy targeting cargo ships and smaller dhows off the Horn of Africa has returned to levels not seen in a decade, driven by a convergence of factors including disruptions to the shipping industry caused by the US-Israeli war against Iran and a resurgence of political instability in Somalia. Since late April there have been eight hijackings by Somali pirates, including two within the space of a fortnight in August : one targeting an oil tanker with ties to Iran, the other a Cameroon-flagged vessel, the Lutuf, carrying military equipment for Turkey. items.summary: US strikes perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, Iranian state media reports The United States targeted the perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant on Thursday, Iranian state media reported, citing Ehsan Jahanian, deputy governor of Bushehr province. Jahanian said several areas across the province were targeted, including the area around the nuclear plant, a military base in the town of Choghadak and a fishing pier in southern Bushehr. He said there were no immediate reports of casualties. Residents in Choghadak, located just over 20km (12 miles) from the Bushehr plant, reported hearing several explosions. The Bushehr facility, Iran’s only civilian nuclear power plant, has previously been affected by strikes in the area during the ongoing Middle East war.

items.summary: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran Iran has warned that it will take reciprocal action if the UN nuclear watchdog adopts a resolution against Tehran, foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on Monday. Speaking at a press briefing, Baghaei criticised European states seeking a resolution against Iran, calling their approach “irrational” given that the ongoing US-Iran war has made several Iranian nuclear facilities inaccessible to international inspectors. His comments come as the US, Britain, France and Germany push for a resolution at the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) over Iran’s lack of cooperation and access to its nuclear sites. Iran has restricted IAEA access to facilities affected by previous strikes, arguing that normal safeguarding arrangements have become impractical under wartime conditions. The dispute has deepened concerns over the status of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile and the international community’s ability to verify the nature of its nuclear programme.

He was full of jokes and promise for the future. Massie said he was not interested in mourning the defeat and declared that he was, in a way, happy he had lost. items.title: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?
items.summary: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US? Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK . Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas. “I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved." The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran . items.summary: Está lejos, Amritsar. Miles de kilómetros separan la capital española de esta ciudad de la India, en la que se levanta el corazón espiritual del sijismo, una religión nacida de un acercamiento de posturas entre el hinduismo y el islam. Cada día, los sij de esta región se reúnen para comer en la monumental infraestructura que constituye el Templo Dorado, donde llenan sus bandejas sin coste ni distinción por edad, género o religión. Lo mismo sucede, en proporciones contenidas, en una nave industrial de Villaverde que esconde el único templo sij de la capital, el Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib de Madrid. Con el mismo espíritu que en la India, pero en esplendor y dimensiones reducidos, este lugar ofrece comidas gratuitas cada domingo a unas pocas decenas de personas.Laura, madrileña de Las Rozas y bautizada en el catolicismo, es una habitual en el lugar desde que, hace más de un año, un viaje a la India despertó en ella una nueva forma de concebir su fe. «Aquí aprendo cómo llegar a dios, que es el mismo para todos», sostiene. items.summary: Fresh Yemen clashes kill more than 60, including 26 soldiers Fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the country's Houthi rebels killed more than 60 people on Saturday, including civilians, medical and military sources told AFP. The renewed clashes in Yemen's southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire. According to three Yemeni military sources, 26 government troops were killed during several hours of fighting in the country's southwest, while medical and military sources from the Iran-backed Houthis said 31 rebel fighters were killed. One medical source in the government-held city of Taiz said a missile strike also killed six civilians travelling by bus and wounded seven others. De afspraken zijn nog niet bindend, maar kunnen leiden tot internationale juridisch bindende afspraken en uiteindelijk misschien zelfs tot een nieuw verdrag. items.summary: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports The Pentagon has begun subjecting senior military officials to lie-detector tests as part of an investigation into who leaked details about US munitions stockpiles, US media reported. Reports in July said the US was rationing some munitions, particularly missile interceptors, amid concerns over supplies following months of war with Iran. Trump administration officials strongly rejected the claims. President Donald Trump said the US had "a lot of ammunition, different types", while acknowledging that the military would like more of "some of the more sophisticated stuff". The New York Times reported late on Friday that around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff, the Pentagon’s planning and advisory body, were being required to undergo polygraph tests as part of an investigation into the leak.

items.summary: England’s manager Thomas Tuchel called the officiating ‘just not good enough’ in the fiery last-16 tie. Now Alireza Faghani gives his version of events It was 6pm on 5 July in Mexico City, and Alireza Faghani, a 48-year-old Australian-Iranian, was asleep in the locker room, snoring. His assistants had turned the music down. Had it not been for the muffled roar of nearly 90,000 fans through the concrete walls of the Estadio Azteca, he could have slept until the following morning. Faghani was the referee for Mexico v England in the last 16 at the 2026 World Cup. Mexico hadn’t lost a competitive game at the Azteca since 2013, at least in part because they’re used to the conditions. Situated 2,240 metres above sea level, the air contains less oxygen. Four vessels entered the Middle East Gulf and one exited, using a mix of Iranian, Omani and negotiated routes. Two of the crossings involved shadow vessels, while one involved a sanctioned vessel. Kpler said the figure remained preliminary, noting that additional “dark” crossings could be retrospectively identified and added as new confirmation data becomes available. Activity through the Bab el-Mandeb was comparatively stable, with 35 confirmed crossings, up 2.9 percent day on day. Nineteen vessels entered the Red Sea and 16 exited. No dark transits were recorded, while the International Maritime Organization verified no additional attacks. items.title: US sanctions on Iran hit three Turkish entities
items.summary: US sanctions on Iran hit three Turkish entities The US has targeted three Turkey-based entitites in a new round of Iran-related sanctions issued on Friday. According to the US Treasury Department, the entities targeted are Golden Global Portfoy Yonetimi Anonim Sirketi, Golden Global Varlik Kiralama Anonim Sirketi, and Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi. The move is the latest in the Trump administration's campaign to economically pressure Tehran six months into Washington's war on Iran, which has pushed energy prices higher worldwide. Diesel prices at home in the US are at an all-time high. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who last month announced an “economic onslaught” against Iran's financial links around the world, has said Washington is seeking to force Tehran back to the negotiating table, Reuters reported.

clusters.headline: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN

items.title: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN
items.summary: World food prices at highest since 2022, says UN World food prices rose in August to their highest since late 2022, impacted partly by the war on Iran, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Friday. Extreme heat and drought in Europe, the threat of a severe El Nino weather pattern and trade upheaval caused by the Ukraine and Iran wars have unsettled agricultural markets, pushing grain prices to three-year highs and sugar to a one-year peak, the agency said. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded food commodities, averaged 133.3 points in August, up from July's revised reading of 130.8. That was the highest score since November 2022, though nearly 17 percent below a record peak from March 2022, after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Reuters reported. Escalating attacks in the Black Sea have curtailed grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, while the war on Iran is still straining flows of fertiliser for crops.

Driscoll’s departure came following reports of increasing tensions with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth as well as signs of unease in the Pentagon over how the Trump administration is prosecuting the war on Iran. The way their stories would cross, then diverge, reveals the cruel arbitrariness of the UK asylum system in general, and the government’s controversial one in, one out scheme in particular. Before he left Iran, Aso, 28, had converted from Islam to Christianity, putting his life in imminent danger. “I had to keep my conversion to Christianity a secret,” he says. “I knew if I was caught, I risked being executed by the Iranian regime … one of my relatives, who I trusted, paid smugglers to get me out last November.” Continue reading...

Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. "Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president. "I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. Van januari tot en met augustus werden ruim 22.000 leningen verstrekt. In heel 2025 waren dat er 21.000. "De aanvragen begonnen toen heel scherp te stijgen." Die stijging zette het hele voorjaar tot de zomer door, zegt Huiberts. items.title: Can 'America First' survive Trump's war-first presidency?
items.summary: In a Thursday address at the GOP midterm convention that exalted President Donald Trump and demeaned his opponents as “extremists who openly hate our nation,” Vice President JD Vance hardly spoke about foreign policy. He did not mention the war in Iran directly, and he only brought up foreign policy as an example of an issue that divides the party’s base. He urged voters not to “throw the baby out with the bathwater” because “you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here or there.” The acknowledgement of foreign policy as a divisive issue in the MAGA coalition is a stark retreat for Vance, who staked his 2023 endorsement of Trump on the fact that “he started no wars despite enormous pressure from his own party and even members of his own administration,” framing the president’s America First record as a much-needed deviation from decades of bipartisan hawkishness. A few wars later, Vance appears to have backed down from the anti-war aspects of the America First movement. items.title: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'?
items.summary: Opinion: 9/11 at 25: Has the US learned anything from its 'war on terror'? A quarter century is enough time to separate history from hysteria, consequences from intentions and reality from propaganda. On 11 September 2001, nearly 3,000 people were killed in horrific attacks that shocked the United States and the world. The attacks of 9/11 could have been treated as a grave crime requiring an international effort to identify, apprehend and prosecute those responsible. They could also have triggered a serious national debate about why such intense hostility towards the US had developed in many parts of the Muslim-majority world. Instead, the US's political establishment chose a radically different path. President George W Bush famously declared that the terrorists attacked the US because "they hate our freedoms". It was a convenient explanation because it absolved the American foreign policy establishment of any responsibility. items.title: Satellite images show smoke near Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline
items.summary: Satellite images show smoke near Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline Satellite images showed smoke rising near Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, one of the kingdom’s key energy assets, Reuters has reported. The news agency said Saudi authorities did not immediately report any incident at the site. The East-West Pipeline has become increasingly important for Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, enabling state oil giant Aramco to ship crude from the kingdom’s eastern coast to the Red Sea on its western coast. It offers an alternative route for sending crude through the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic global energy chokepoint. items.title: Iran president says he does not favour continuing the war
items.summary: Iran president says he does not favour continuing the war Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he does not support continuing the war, but he stressed that Iran needs to improve its resistance to future challenges so that it does not have to negotiate from a position of weakness. Speaking to heads of the country’s leading universities, Pezeshkian said universities should support the government across areas including the economy, management, culture and literature, ISNA reported. Pezeshkian also called for greater involvement of students in tackling national issues. “We must make sure that instead of engaging in protest, they engage in solving problems,” he said. The president said he had “no political angle with anyone”, adding, “Whoever helps us solve the country’s problems, with whatever political viewpoint, I accept.” “Economic measures must take into account the country’s conditions, otherwise they will lead to negative results and losses instead of addressing the issues,” Pezeshkian said.

The latest flare-up began with a US strike on Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces in southern Iran, according to Iranian accounts. Irak had niets met de aanslagen te maken. Toch werd het land een belangrijk strijdtoneel van de Amerikaanse War on Terror . Nu, 25 jaar later, kent het Midden-Oosten een erfenis die verbonden is met wat er lang na die vreselijke dag in de VS gebeurde. Op beelden is te zien dat er enorme explosies waren bij de strategisch gelegen Ali Taher-heuvelrug. Die ligt op 15 kilometer van de grens met Israël. Volgens Libanese veiligheidsbronnen, die persbureau Reuters in juli sprak, heeft Hezbollah in het gebied een ondergronds commandocentrum en wapenopslagplaatsen. De heuvel en de omringende plekken zijn een van de meest betwiste gebieden in de de huidige oorlog tussen Israël en Hezbollah. Volgens Israël is met de aanval "de operationele controle van de Ali Taher-heuvelrug bereikt, zowel bovengronds als ondergronds". Het leger bracht beelden naar buiten van de explosie: Bij de aanval werd 1100 ton aan explosieven gebruikt, meldt het Israëlische leger. De schokken waren voelbaar in heel Zuid-Libanon en zelfs in de hoofdstad Beiroet, die op ongeveer 70 kilometer afstand ligt. items.summary: Iran dismisses IAEA resolution, says nonproliferation accusations political Iran has dismissed a resolution passed by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which accuses Tehran of failing to comply with its nuclear nonproliferation commitments and refers the matter to the UN Security Council. “Renewed accusations against Iran’s peaceful nuclear program are political and not technical in nature,” Iran's UN ambassador, Gholamhossein Darzi, said in a letter addressed to the Security Council president, IRNA reported. “The Islamic Republic of Iran categorically rejects the baseless accusations and distortions raised by some members in this meeting regarding Iran’s peaceful nuclear program,” Darzi said. The IAEA resolution, which is backed by the US and its key European allies, expressed “grave concern” over Iran’s “continued noncompliance” with its obligations under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

items.summary: The territorial dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands (or Islas Malvinas in Spanish) continues to escalate. Last week, Argentine President Javier Milei, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, announced a series of new measures aimed at pressuring Britain over the future of the islands. The most significant announcement was of new sanctions on companies involved in oil extraction in the waters around the Falklands, which Argentina has long claimed as its own. Argentina’s attempt to prevent the exploitation of the Falklands’ natural resources is a reminder that beneath the often farcical relitigating of sovereignty claims dating back to the 18th century is a very modern geopolitical conflict with real stakes for energy and maritime resources. Yet what was most remarkable about Milei’s announcement was what Milei did not announce — namely, a shift in U.S. policy regarding the Falklands. items.title: Iranian strikes damaged multiple aircraft at Jordan base, report says
items.summary: Iranian strikes damaged multiple aircraft at Jordan base, report says Iranian strikes damaged multiple American military aircraft this week on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, a US official told Reuters. The US military, the highest-funded in the world, suffered material damage even before Iran's strikes on Tuesday. This includes the destruction of more than two dozen drones, Iran striking fighter jets, and aircraft being lost to accidents. According to a May report from the Congressional Research Service, 42 US military aircraft had already been lost or damaged in the conflict. Since the Iran war started in February, 18 US service members have been killed and over 800 injured. A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said Iran's attack hit one A-10 Thunderbolt II, known as the Warthog, leaving it with a missing wing, while roughly eight F-15s sustained light damage and were returned to service. Iran's strike on the US base in Jordan came after US forces said they destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers. Report by Reuters

items.title: US diesel prices surpass $6 a gallon for first time as oil hits highest since May
items.summary: US diesel prices surpass $6 a gallon for first time as oil hits highest since May The US national average price of diesel on Thursday surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time ever, according to price tracker GasBuddy, as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russia’s refineries have squeezed supply. The latest surge in fuel costs is adding to inflationary pressures that have already strained consumers and businesses this year, creating a political headache for President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers as they seek to defend thin congressional majorities in November's midterm elections. Crude oil futures on Thursday hit their highest level since mid-May. Brent settled at $107.63 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate futures at $102.48 a barrel.

items.summary: IRGC says it targeted unmanned US sea drone in Hormuz Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Thursday its navy targeted a US unmanned surface vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. "The Navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted a Saildrone Explorer-type unmanned surface vessel in the Strait of Hormuz area, the IRGC said in a statement carried by its Sepah news outlet. IRGC added that the sea drone had been used in the region by the US Fifth Fleet stationed in Bahrain. Washington has previously used Saildrone Explorer USs to gather data and images in the Gulf. The sea drones run on solar and wind energy and can be deployed on missions in the ocean for up to one year. Iran on Wednesday said it captured an unmanned US submarine drone. The US military said one of its underwater drones had "malfunctioned".

Iran told the Houthis last week to escalate their attacks on Saudi Arabia, a close US ally, and promised more funding, weapons and senior officers to help them do so, two Iranian sources said. Several senior Revolutionary Guards commanders had already travelled to Yemen to oversee and command Houthi attacks directed against Saudi Arabia after weeks of discussions over military strategy, a regional diplomat briefed by Tehran said. A third Iranian source, an official, said Iran had held several meetings with allies including the Houthis and that the move on Mocha was a Houthi rather than Iranian decision. However, it had helped Iran by putting upward pressure on oil prices and hurting the United States and Saudi Arabia, the official added. Reporting by Reuters

items.title: Olivier Grondeau, ancien otage en Iran : «La poésie, c'est ce qui m'a fait tenir»
items.summary: Olivier Grondeau a passé deux ans et demi en prison en Iran. Son nom est moins connu que ceux d’otages dont le cas a été médiatisé. Son histoire est assez proche. Arrêté à Chiraz le 12 octobre 2022, à l’époque des manifestations suivant la mort de Jina Mahsa Amini, il a été libéré en mars 2025. Il n’avait décidé de parler de sa situation que quelques mois plus tôt. Olivier Grondeau est un voyageur à tout petit budget, un poète, un grand lecteur, un ancien champion de scrabble. C’est son esprit, son humour, son imagination qui l’ont aidé à tenir. Il le raconte dans un livre publié chez l’iconoclaste : « Joseph dans la nuit »

items.title: Political Instability Meets Fiscal Limits: Is France the Euro’s Next Big Stress Test?
items.summary: With around half a year remaining before the next presidential election, France is in danger of becoming a stress test for the eurozone: a political crisis, a deteriorating fiscal position and growing market doubts about the country’s ability to finance its mounting debt burden are all converging. France faces a significant structural imbalance in its public finances. The budget deficit exceeds 5 per cent of GDP , while public expenditure stands at around 57 per cent of GDP. At the same time, public debt is rising steadily and could, without sufficient fiscal consolidation measures, exceed 130 per cent of GDP by 2030 . The interest burden on public debt is rising rapidly and could rise to more than 120 billion euros, equivalent to 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2030. The central challenge, however, may not lie in the fiscal arithmetic of the budget, but in the political capacity to address it. On the one hand, the costs of social welfare expenditure are no longer sustainable; on the other, the majority of the population continues to demand more state intervention. Symposium: What I miss most about pre-9/11 America
items.summary: While it is somewhat cliche to say that the “whole world changed” after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, it does not detract from the reality of the statement. In numerous tangible ways, the culture, security, and politics of the nation were never the same after al-Qaida hijackers in passenger planes left nearly 3,000 people dead in smoldering ruins across lower Manhattan, the Pentagon, and a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. For many of us who lived through it all, a quarter century has passed in a blink, while at the same time the pre-9/11 Washington era paradoxically seems so far away, and perhaps softened a bit by wistfulness and nostalgia. Conversely, the “post” era is pockmarked by wars, and an expansion of the national security state that was unimaginable a generation ago. Those born too early to witness the events of that day know nothing other than the current atmosphere of hyper-securitization and political polarization. items.title: Oil prices breach $100 as Iran-US attacks escalate
items.summary: Oil prices breach $100 as Iran-US attacks escalate Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel on Wednesday to settle at their highest close since late May after Iran and the US struck tankers in the biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began. Front-month Brent crude futures settled up $3.29, or 3.4%, at $101.21 a barrel, after touching a high of $101.58. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was up $3.02, or 3.25%, at $96.05 a barrel. Both benchmarks closed at their highest since May 22. Since late May, oil benchmarks have generally traded well below the $100-per-barrel psychological threshold, reflecting expectations that the conflict would remain on a low simmer. Report by Reuters

items.title: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports
items.summary: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict could stretch through his term, WSJ reports Top White House advisers, including vice president JD Vance and secretary of state Marco Rubio, have privately warned president Donald Trump that the conflict with Iran could extend through the remainder of his presidency, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials. The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The advisers told Trump in private discussions in the Oval Office and the Situation Room that Tehran could continue to resist US pressure, potentially prolonging the conflict beyond Inauguration Day in January 2029, the Journal added. The reported warning contrasts with Trump's own public remarks about the war. The president said on Wednesday he expected the war to end "immediately after" the US midterm elections in November, arguing that Iran was trying to influence the vote but would be unable to sustain its resistance much longer. Trump also acknowledged diplomatic talks are still a possibility but were not preferred. Report by Reuters

items.summary: Trump says Iran war will end 'immediately' after midterm elections President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he believes the Iran war will end "immediately" after the US midterm elections in November. "I think the war will end immediately after the election" because Iran "can't hold out any longer," Trump told journalists, accusing Tehran of being "desperate to try and affect" the vote. Asked about the possibility of resumed talks with Tehran, Trump said "we’re not looking for it, to be honest", adding that "they have very little country left right now", but "a negotiation could possibly happen". He also reiterated his intention to prohibit Iran from having nuclear weapons.

items.summary: In 1973, after it was discovered that the U.S. had secretly bombed Cambodia, Congress took action. In an effort to assert its power over matters of war and peace, Congress pushed through the War Powers Resolution despite then-President Richard Nixon’s veto, and it has been law ever since. Unfortunately, congressional enforcement of the War Powers Resolution has been mixed. In 2026 alone, Congress has put forward some 19 war powers resolutions in an attempt to rein in hostilities in Iran, Venezuela, Cuba, and Lebanon. So far, none of these resolutions has stopped a conflict. Take Iran, for example. There have been eight votes to end the war, seven of which failed. Just one of these passed and only because Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) changed course after losing his primary to a challenger endorsed by President Donald Trump, giving him leeway to vote against the bulk of the Republican Party. Cassidy’s move highlights one of the main problems with the War Powers Resolution: too many of our elected officials cast votes for political gain, not American interests. items.title: ‘One day the Taliban will need women to be educated’: three sisters on being forced back to Afghanistan
items.summary: Shallah, Fatimah and Maahi are among hundreds of thousands of Afghan women and girls deported from Iran and Pakistan in the past year to a life of severe restrictions It was a warm summer afternoon on 15 August 2021 when the Taliban entered Kabul and changed the lives of millions. Shallah*, then 16, watched the news at home on the Afghan TV channel Tolo news. She ran crying to the garden, to tell her mother that Afghanistan had fallen. Her younger sister, Fatimah*, then 11, was at her cousin’s house, where her aunt told her the news. At the time, she says, she did not understand what a takeover meant, or who the Taliban were. Her elder sister, Maahi*, then 22, was well aware of the consequences and remembers her hands shaking at work as she read the news on her phone, on Facebook pages of Afghan news. Continue reading...

items.summary: Na de nieuwe aanvallen van de Verenigde Staten en Iran zijn de olieprijzen opnieuw gestegen. De prijs van een vat Brent-olie kwam vanochtend boven de 100 dollar uit. Dat is voor het eerst sinds juli. Een vat Brent-olie is inmiddels bijna 60 procent duurder dan begin dit jaar. Door de aanvallen tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran is er onrust op de oliemarkt. Het aanhoudende geweld vergroot de zorgen over mogelijke verstoringen van de olie-export uit de regio. De Amerikaanse bank Goldman Sachs heeft gewaarschuwd dat de olieprijs kan oplopen naar 120 dollar per vat als de aanvallen aanhouden. De stijgende olieprijs is ook al te merken aan de pomp. De adviesprijs voor een liter benzine ligt nu rond de 2,72 euro.

items.title: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États
items.summary: La sortie mondiale du pétrole pourrait entraîner des conflits, des migrations et des bouleversements économiques selon une étude du groupe de réflexion E3G publiée mardi 8 septembre. L’utilisation du pétrole est en déclin dans de nombreux pays, avec la croissance des énergies renouvelables, et les effets de la guerre en Iran qui a limité l’offre et fait flamber les prix. Et cette stagnation va obliger les producteurs à rechercher un bassin d’acheteurs en déclin. Des pays comme le Nigeria, l’Iran, l’Angola et l’Algérie font partie des pays qui seront gravement touchés, car ils dépendent fortement des revenus pétroliers pour financer leurs services publics. Sans aide internationale, ils ne pourront pas amortir le choc alertent les experts.

Dat blijkt uit cijfers van het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS). Door de aanhoudende droogte daalde de vaardiepte, waardoor schepen minder zwaar beladen konden worden. In totaal werd er 21,8 miljoen ton vervoerd. Dat is het laagste vervoerde gewicht in de maand augustus in de afgelopen vijftien jaar. In augustus bedroeg het gemiddelde gewicht per schip zo'n 1299 ton, terwijl dat normaal rond de 1500 ton ligt. Het is niet de eerste keer dat het vervoerde gewicht in de binnenvaart fors afneemt door lage waterstanden: dit gebeurde in 2018 en 2022 ook. Verschillen Naar bijna elk land werd er minder vervoerd via de binnenvaart. Het vervoer tussen Nederland en Duitsland nam het sterkst af. Er ging bijna 40 procent minder gewicht aan goederen naar Duitsland, en omgekeerd kwam er voor een kleine 50 procent minder naar Nederland. items.title: Trump denials can't hide billions in US weapons sent to Ukraine

Her central argument is that the conflict has created a problem of face-saving as much as military strategy. The US faces rising economic and electoral costs, while Iran confronts shortages, inflation, domestic dissent and intensified repression. Neither side, in her assessment, can plausibly claim success.

items.title: 25 years after 9/11, the US still doesn't know 'why they hate us'
items.summary: Twenty-five years ago, 19 hijackers took control of four American airliners and crashed them into symbols of American power, killing upwards of 3000 people. The American population watched the events unfold in real time. It was an emotionally jarring event that changed the country. In some respects, the events of 9/11 needed no explanation. The destruction of the World Trade Center buildings and the massive, and random, loss of life were horrifying to all. The meaning of the attacks, however – and the motivations of the hijackers – were less clear. The effort to explain the motives behind the attack, and to understand “why they hate us,” brought a pre-existing debate over Islamist militancy to the center of American public life. In the decade leading up to 9/11, the Washington policy community had been divided over how to deal with the Islamist movement and particularly those extremists who sought to use violence to impose a narrow vision of religious orthodoxy upon reluctant societies. items.title: Somali piracy was under control. Then came the Iran war.
items.summary: From the start, the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has been a story of unintended consequences. Contrary to President Donald Trump’s hopes for a quick victory, the conflict has morphed into a sustained crisis, one that has driven up oil prices, driven down tourism in the Middle East, and reshaped the region’s geopolitical map. Now, a new unintended consequence has emerged: the return of piracy to Somalia’s coasts. This shift, which comes after a decade of quiet, threatens some of the world’s most important shipping lanes and the interests of the United States and its allies. Pirates have attacked at least 15 vessels in the region this year, a sharp uptick from the five attacks that occurred last year, according to data from the International Maritime Organization. The renewed criminal activity has led to extended hostage situations, including one ongoing seizure of an oil tanker and its crew. A controversial operation to free the MV LATUF, carried out by Somali forces and the Turkish navy late last month, raised questions about whether a ransom was paid. items.summary: US strikes perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, Iranian state media reports The United States targeted the perimeter of Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant on Thursday, Iranian state media reported, citing Ehsan Jahanian, deputy governor of Bushehr province. Jahanian said several areas across the province were targeted, including the area around the nuclear plant, a military base in the town of Choghadak and a fishing pier in southern Bushehr. He said there were no immediate reports of casualties. Residents in Choghadak, located just over 20km (12 miles) from the Bushehr plant, reported hearing several explosions. The Bushehr facility, Iran’s only civilian nuclear power plant, has previously been affected by strikes in the area during the ongoing Middle East war.

items.title: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran
items.summary: Iran warns of retaliation if IAEA adopts resolution against Tehran Iran has warned that it will take reciprocal action if the UN nuclear watchdog adopts a resolution against Tehran, foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on Monday. Speaking at a press briefing, Baghaei criticised European states seeking a resolution against Iran, calling their approach “irrational” given that the ongoing US-Iran war has made several Iranian nuclear facilities inaccessible to international inspectors. His comments come as the US, Britain, France and Germany push for a resolution at the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) over Iran’s lack of cooperation and access to its nuclear sites. Iran has restricted IAEA access to facilities affected by previous strikes, arguing that normal safeguarding arrangements have become impractical under wartime conditions. The dispute has deepened concerns over the status of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile and the international community’s ability to verify the nature of its nuclear programme.

items.title: Hormuz traffic drops to lowest since May
items.summary: Hormuz traffic drops to lowest since May An average of 10 commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz daily over the past 10 days, marking the lowest traffic in the waterway since May, shipping data by Kpler on Monday showed. The 10-day moving average was 10 on Sunday, down from more than nearly 13 on Saturday. Meanwhile, only two vessels passed through the strait on Saturday while six others went through on Sunday, mostly using the Iranian route.

items.title: Iran turns to land trade routes to counter maritime blockade
items.summary: Iran turns to land trade routes to counter maritime blockade We have more from Iran’s top security official, Mohsen Rezaei. Rezaei says Tehran has started activating overland trade corridors to reduce its dependence on shipping and counter the maritime blockade. He pointed to Iran’s borders with 15 neighbouring countries, arguing that its geographical position gives it alternatives to sea-based commerce. Rezaei also said Iran and Oman had agreed on a new international corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran would oversee. “The new international corridor that Iran manages has been determined with the Omani brothers and will be announced in the coming days,” Rezaei said, according to state media.

The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?
items.summary: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US? Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK . Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas. “I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved." The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran . items.title: De un chalé de Arturo Soria a un polígono de Villaverde: viaje a las religiones que menos fieles profesan en Madrid
items.summary: Está lejos, Amritsar. Miles de kilómetros separan la capital española de esta ciudad de la India, en la que se levanta el corazón espiritual del sijismo, una religión nacida de un acercamiento de posturas entre el hinduismo y el islam. Cada día, los sij de esta región se reúnen para comer en la monumental infraestructura que constituye el Templo Dorado, donde llenan sus bandejas sin coste ni distinción por edad, género o religión. Lo mismo sucede, en proporciones contenidas, en una nave industrial de Villaverde que esconde el único templo sij de la capital, el Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib de Madrid. items.title: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes
items.summary: Iran condemns US attacks on commercial vessels as war crimes Iran has accused the United States of violating international law by attacking its commercial vessels and imposing a naval blockade against the country. “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the aggressive US action of attacking Iranian commercial vessels,” the Foreign Ministry said. Tehran described the strikes as part of Washington’s wider military campaign and “economic war” against Iran. It said the attacks violated the UN Charter and endangered international peace, security and commercial shipping. The ministry pledged to “firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests” against US aggression, state-sponsored terrorism, the continuing blockade and the “harassment of commercial ships”. It added that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from continued US “aggressive and interventionist actions” in the region.

items.title: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports
items.summary: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak investigation: reports The Pentagon has begun subjecting senior military officials to lie-detector tests as part of an investigation into who leaked details about US munitions stockpiles, US media reported. Reports in July said the US was rationing some munitions, particularly missile interceptors, amid concerns over supplies following months of war with Iran. Trump administration officials strongly rejected the claims. President Donald Trump said the US had "a lot of ammunition, different types", while acknowledging that the military would like more of "some of the more sophisticated stuff". The New York Times reported late on Friday that around 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff, the Pentagon’s planning and advisory body, were being required to undergo polygraph tests as part of an investigation into the leak.

items.title: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers
items.summary: US military says it has destroyed three Iranian oil tankers The US military said it had struck and destroyed three oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) after US warships came under Iranian fire. "Following Iran’s failed attacks, CENTCOM permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask," Central Command (Centcom) said in a statement on X. "American forces also completely destroyed the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo … in the Gulf of Oman, striking the vessel in multiple critical locations to render it inoperable after the crew was directed to abandon ship," it continued. Video released by Centcom showed huge fireballs and thick plumes of flames erupting as projectiles struck the vessels. The three ships targeted were "part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies", it said. "Iran has no means by which to defend them," it added.

items.summary: US, allies push IAEA board to report Iran to UN Security Council The United States, Britain, France and Germany are seeking a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog's board next week reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years, according to diplomats and the proposed text seen by Reuters. If passed, the resolution would follow up on one adopted on June 12 of last year declaring Iran in breach of its non-proliferation obligations for not fully cooperating with an investigation into uranium traces found at undeclared sites. Israel started bombing Iran's nuclear facilities the next day, soon joined by the US Iran's uranium-enrichment plants were destroyed or badly damaged. Iran has not let International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors return to the bombed sites since then or verify what remains of its stocks of enriched uranium, some of which was enriched to up to 60 percent purity, a short step from weapons grade. (Reporting by Reuters)
